title: Dimensional Monitoring Defunding Act
description: Proposed the immediate 60% reduction in funding for the 'Eyes of the Ring' dimensional monitoring stations, citing high maintenance costs and lack of active threats.
aftermath: The act passed by a razor-thin margin. Three months later, the First Rift Leak occurred in the Subspace Sector, which many attribute to reduced sensor coverage. The Iron Pact utilized the resulting chaos to sell their own private security services.
waluigiComment: They didn't defund it because it was expensive. They defunded it because the stations were pointed at Iron Pact shipyard secret projects. Efficiency! Crime pays better when nobody is looking.

title: Sovereignty Exception for Pre-emptive Stabilization
description: A legal amendment allowing member nations to cross borders without a formal declaration of war if imminent social collapse is detected in a neighbor. Designed to prevent another Blorbs outbreak.
aftermath: Passed under intense lobbying. Within a year, this was used as the legal justification for the Stabilization of the East Glaze regions, effectively a quiet annexation by the Empire.
waluigiComment: It's a stabilization the same way a boot stabilizes an ant. They even convinced the Progressive Bloc to vote for it by calling it a humanitarian intervention. Everyone is so easily fooled by a good font.

title: Emergency Taxation of Neutral Trade Routes
description: Levying a 15% toll on all non-aligned merchant vessels passing through the Great Glaze Bridge to fund Congress security forces.
aftermath: Caused a massive trade strike. Smaller nations and the Non-Aligned bloc are currently suing the Congress in its own court, which is conveniently funded by the same tax.
waluigiComment: Finally, the Congress is becoming a real government: they've learned how to steal from people who don't have a seat at the table. Waluigi is almost proud.

title: Recognition of the Internet Federation as Full Member
description: Whether digital sovereignty constitutes recognized territorial control for full membership purposes. Established the precedent that territory need not be physical.
aftermath: Established digital sovereignty as recognized territorial control. Implications for subsequent membership applications nobody anticipated. Internet Federation has exploited holographic attendance precedent aggressively.
waluigiComment: The right decision made for slightly wrong reasons. Several delegates voted yes because they didn't understand what digital territory meant and were embarrassed to ask.

title: Dimensional Barrier Monitoring Resolution
description: Framework for monitoring and reporting dimensional barrier integrity across member territories. Direct response to Chaos Heart Crisis legacy of weakened planar boundaries.
aftermath: Committee produced exactly three reports before being quietly defunded in 1031 BF when Regal Empire objected to monitoring over their territory. The Raventree Fracture of 1040 BF would have had 14 years of baseline data if the committee existed. Instead responders work from nothing.
waluigiComment: Waluigi supported this enthusiastically and was told to sit down. Waluigi raised his hand anyway. Waluigi's hand did not count. Waluigi considers this a procedural injustice. Waluigi is STILL angry about this.

title: Species Recognition Compact
description: Minimum standards for legal recognition of sapient species. Members must recognize personhood of any species recognized by at least three other members. Prohibits treating recognized species as property, livestock, or pest populations.
aftermath: Most consequential resolution for ordinary people. Established that sapience is sapience regardless of species. Not perfectly enforced but created legal language advocates use and standards that did not exist before 1026 BF.
waluigiComment: This is what the Congress is for. Not perfect. Not enough. But this resolution has saved lives that would have been lost without it. Waluigi will defend it.

title: Trade Route Protections
proposedBy: Iron Hills Dwarven Holds / Beanbean Kingdom (joint)
description: Shared standards for protection of trade routes through multiple member territories. Reduced cross-border tariff disputes, established arbitration, created Trans-Doughnut Trade Registry.
aftermath: Easiest vote of the session. Money motivates consensus when nothing else does. Trans-Doughnut Trade Registry still operates today and is arguably the Congress's most practically successful creation.
waluigiComment: Even Wario's fake representative voted for this one. When everyone can count the coins, cooperation is easy. It's when the costs are moral rather than financial that the counting gets harder.

title: Fawful Condemnation Resolution
description: Formal condemnation of Fawful's aggressive territorial actions, biological warfare through contaminated food distribution, and unauthorized seizure of sovereign military infrastructure.
aftermath: Low approval margin embarrassing for Mushroom Kingdom. Multiple delegates objected to naming specific actors in founding documents. Beanbean Kingdom abstained. Fawful survived condemnation by being alive while everyone congratulated themselves on paperwork.
waluigiComment: The Congress's first named condemnation should not have been of a defeated actor. It should have been saved for when it was needed.

title: Observer Status Admissions Batch
description: Admitted twelve factions as non-voting observers including Mages Guild, Iron Legion, Freelancer Underworld, Koopa Troop, Team Rocket, Rakasha Clans, Peach Loyalists, DK Crew, Yoshi Clans, Data Merchants, Cybernetic Collectives, and Warioland.
aftermath: Most admissions uncontroversial. Iron Legion admission was unanimous which in retrospect was suspicious. Wario's representative speech contained 11 factual inaccuracies.
waluigiComment: Everyone who might object to Iron Legion observer status was also either allied with or intimidated by the Iron Legion. The unanimous vote should have been a warning. Nobody was warned.

title: Equestria Seat-in-Trust Resolution
description: Hold Equestria's potential seat in trust, formally recognizing a pony-nation seat exists and will be available when Equestria chooses to join.
aftermath: Seat has been held in trust for fourteen years. Equestria has not joined. Celestia's solar monarchy continues to describe the Congress as harmonically misaligned.
waluigiComment: Waluigi is not optimistic about what form the threat that finally brings Equestria in will take.

title: Greenskin Territories Membership Application
description: Application from the Greenskin Territories for full membership. Contested on grounds that a rotating warchief council does not constitute stable governance. Counter-argued that stability of the council as an institution is more relevant than identity of its current holder.
aftermath: Narrow approval. Set precedent that institutional continuity matters more than governmental form. Greenskin Territories have since been the most consistent bloc vote against any resolution that increases central Congress authority over member militaries, for obvious reasons.
waluigiComment: The Greenskin delegates are the most honest people in the chamber. They want what they want and they say so. Waluigi finds this refreshing after forty minutes of Gondor's representative explaining why Gondor's interests are everyone's interests.

title: Freelancer Underworld Accountability Compact
description: Required the Freelancer Underworld observer delegation to submit annual activity reports disclosing operations conducted within member territories and agree to basic conflict-of-interest rules preventing delegates from simultaneously holding active contracts against member nations.
aftermath: Failed badly. Eleven member nations voted against because they had active Freelancer Underworld contracts they did not want disclosed. Nobody admitted this. The stated reason was national sovereignty. The real reason was embarrassment.
waluigiComment: The vote against transparency was itself a transparency problem. Waluigi has a list of who voted no. The list is unsurprising.

title: Blorbs Outbreak Emergency Response Framework
description: Established shared protocols for cross-border medical emergency response following the Blorbs outbreak. Included provisions for emergency border crossing rights for medical teams, shared supply stockpile requirements, and mandatory reporting of outbreak indicators.
aftermath: One of the most successful resolutions in Congress history. Actually implemented. Actually followed. The shared stockpile provision was controversial until the 1034 BF secondary outbreak when Yoshi's Island received emergency medical supplies from three nations within 48 hours. The four abstentions were nations who wanted stronger mandatory provisions.
waluigiComment: When the threat is biological and visible and has already killed people everyone knows, cooperation happens. The lesson the Congress refuses to learn is that this is the template, not the exception.

title: Warioland Full Membership Application
description: Warioland's second membership application following rejection of the first on grounds that the submitted territorial documentation was partially forged. Second application included certified surveyor reports.
aftermath: Passed despite ongoing concerns about Warioland's compliance with Species Recognition Compact regarding Wario's treatment of his own workers. Wario attended the admission ceremony, ate most of the ceremonial catering, and gave a speech that was primarily about himself.
waluigiComment: Waluigi abstained. Not because Warioland should not be a member. Because Wario should not be the one running it. These are different positions. Waluigi holds both of them simultaneously.

title: Rakasha Clans Census Dispute Resolution
description: The Rakasha Clans contested their population tier classification as Small, arguing their nomadic population was systematically undercounted because census methodology assumed fixed residence. Requested reclassification to Medium tier.
aftermath: Failed on a bloc vote by every nation that feared nomadic-population methodology changes would affect their own census numbers. The Rakasha Clans' complaint was legitimate. The methodology is still broken. Several other nations with mobile or dispersed populations are also undercounted and have not bothered to raise the issue because they watched what happened here.
waluigiComment: The nations who voted no were not wrong that changing the methodology would affect their numbers. They were wrong about why that was a reason to vote no. Accurate numbers are better than convenient numbers. The Congress does not agree.

title: Iron Hills Mining Sovereignty Compact
description: Established that sub-surface mineral rights belong exclusively to the surface territory's governing nation regardless of the depth of extraction or proximity to neighboring territories. Specifically targeted at disputes with the Greenskin Territories over deep-tunnel mining near shared borders.
aftermath: Passed easily because most nations have surface resources they wanted protected. The Greenskin Territories voted against loudly and have not complied quietly. Deep-tunnel disputes continue. The Compact has never been enforced against a nation large enough to make enforcement expensive.
waluigiComment: The Iron Hills delegates arrived with the most comprehensive legal documentation Waluigi has ever seen in a Congress session. Three hundred pages. Cross-referenced. Indexed. They had been preparing this since before the Congress existed. Waluigi is impressed. Waluigi is also slightly afraid.

title: Pokemon League Training Facility Sovereignty Act
description: Whether Pokemon training facilities operating within member nations constituted Pokemon League sovereign territory or were subject to host nation law. Significant implications for taxation, labor standards, and legal jurisdiction over incidents involving Pokemon.
aftermath: Failed comprehensively. Most nations were not willing to cede jurisdictional authority to a foreign body operating within their borders. Pokemon League's legal status within host nations remains a patchwork of bilateral agreements. Some Pokemon trainers operate under League law, some under local law, some under both simultaneously. Several trainers have been arrested in three jurisdictions for the same incident.
waluigiComment: The Pokemon League made a reasonable argument and lost it completely because they framed it as sovereignty rather than consistency. If they had asked for shared jurisdiction they would have gotten something. They asked for exclusive jurisdiction and got nothing. Pride is expensive.

title: Gondor Military Cooperation Treaty
description: Established a framework for military cooperation between member nations in response to coordinated threats. Included provisions for joint command structures, shared intelligence, and mutual defense obligations within defined threat categories.
aftermath: Gondor spent four years lobbying for this and wrote most of the framework themselves. The mutual defense provisions were significantly watered down before passage. Several nations signed with reservations so extensive the reservations are longer than the treaty. Gondor's delegate described the result as a foundation. He was being optimistic.
waluigiComment: Gondor writes military treaties the way Gondor does everything: seriously, thoroughly, and with the implicit assumption that Gondor's military traditions are the default. The other nations noticed this. The watered-down provisions were a direct response to noticing it.

title: Shake Kingdom Agricultural Standards Compact
description: Minimum standards for food safety, agricultural labor conditions, and cross-border food trade certification. The Shake Kingdom's agricultural output feeds significant portions of the Doughnut World and they wanted legal protection for their trade relationships.
aftermath: Near-unanimous. The Shake Kingdom is one of the few nations everyone depends on. Food diplomacy works better than military diplomacy. The single no vote was from a nation whose domestic agricultural lobby objected to the import certification requirements. They have since quietly complied.
waluigiComment: The Shake Kingdom gets things done because they came to the Congress with something everyone needs and asked for something reasonable in return. Waluigi has been recommending this approach to other small nations for years. Several of them have tried it. It works more often than not.

title: DK Crew Island Territory Expansion Recognition
description: Recognition of the DK Crew's expanded territorial claim following reclamation of several island chains previously occupied by Kremling forces. Contested by the Kremling Kingdom which had not officially been recognized by the Congress but argued the territories were disputed.
aftermath: Passed without much debate. The Kremling Kingdom had no representative and no allies willing to argue their case. DK Crew territorial claims recognized. The four no votes were from nations with complicated relationships to the concept of territorial reclamation who did not want to set precedents.
waluigiComment: Donkey Kong attended this session personally. He did not speak. He did not need to. His presence was the argument. Waluigi respects this approach more than he expected to.

title: Mordor Membership Application
description: The most contentious vote in Congress history. Argued across three sessions. Produced the Mordor Compromise establishing enhanced monitoring provisions for members whose governance structures do not include civilian oversight.
aftermath: Congress's greatest achievement and most significant failure simultaneously. Greatest because it established membership requires minimum standards. Failure because those standards were written specifically to accommodate Mordor. Circular table arrangement created so no delegation was technically adjacent to Mordor while all were technically equal.
waluigiComment: If you write minimum standards to accommodate the worst applicant they are not minimum standards. They are maximum tolerance. The Congress knows this. The Congress did it anyway. Waluigi understands why. Waluigi does not approve.

title: Cybernetic Collectives Full Membership Application
description: Application for full membership from the Cybernetic Collectives, a distributed network of augmented and fully synthetic persons claiming sovereign digital and physical territory. Raised philosophical questions about whether a distributed governance structure with no fixed capital constitutes a recognizable state.
aftermath: Controversial but ultimately followed the Internet Federation precedent established in vote 001. The Cybernetic Collectives are the second-smallest delegation by seat count but have more data processing capability than the rest of the Congress combined. Several members find this unsettling and have said so.
waluigiComment: The Cybernetic Collectives delegate gave their opening statement simultaneously in 847 languages. Waluigi was in the room. Waluigi will not pretend it was not impressive. Waluigi will also not pretend it was not slightly threatening.

title: Yoshi Clans Autonomy Recognition
description: Recognition of the Yoshi Clans as distinct autonomous cultural territories within Yoshi's Island sovereignty. Gave the Yoshi Clans a sub-national recognition framework that allowed them to participate in Congress cultural exchanges without full membership.
aftermath: Largely symbolic but created a framework several other nations with restless autonomous regions have since quietly referenced when negotiating their own internal arrangements. The two no votes were from nations who found the precedent of sub-national recognition alarming for their own internal politics.
waluigiComment: The Yoshi Clans eat everything and have survived longer than most of the nations in this chamber. Waluigi respects longevity. Waluigi also respects the diplomatic instinct to ask for recognition rather than independence. The distinction matters.

title: Mages Guild Full Membership Application
description: Application from the Mages Guild for full membership. Technically the Guild spans multiple member territories and does not hold exclusive sovereign territory. Application argued that unique expertise and cross-border mandate constituted functional sovereignty.
aftermath: Failed by one vote. The Mages Guild has not reapplied. They remain as observers and have consistently been the most practically useful advisory body in the Congress despite having no formal voting power. Several member nations have noted the irony that the body with the most expertise has the least formal authority.
waluigiComment: One vote. The nation whose delegate was absent that day has since cycled through three different delegates. None of them know they are the reason the Mages Guild is not a full member. Waluigi knows. Waluigi has not told them. Waluigi is saving this information.

title: Dimensional Monitoring Committee Restructuring
description: Restructuring of the Dimensional Barrier Monitoring Committee that effectively eliminated its funding, staff, and mandate under the guise of jurisdictional concerns over monitoring sovereignty.
aftermath: The committee that would have had 14 years of dimensional barrier data by 1040 BF ceased to function. The Raventree Fracture emergency response works from nothing. Waluigi considers this the Congress's worst vote.
waluigiComment: 847 resolutions. This is the one that will kill people. This is the one that already has. Waluigi raised this issue in 1026. Waluigi was told to sit down. The dimensional fracture does not care who is sitting and who is standing.

title: Freelancer Underworld Charter Compliance Review
description: Formal review of whether the Freelancer Underworld's observer status should be revoked following documented evidence that Freelancer operatives had conducted operations against three member nations while their delegate voted on resolutions affecting those same nations.
aftermath: Failed because nine of the nations who voted no had current or recent Freelancer contracts. The Freelancer Underworld delegate voted on the resolution about themselves. The Congress rules technically permitted this. The Congress rules have not been changed.
waluigiComment: The defendant voted on their own trial. The Congress allowed this. Waluigi would find this farcical if the consequences were not serious. They are serious. Waluigi finds it farcical anyway.

title: Shire Agricultural Preservation Compact
description: Protection of small-scale traditional agricultural practices from being forced out by industrial competition through cross-border trade agreements. Included provisions preventing member nations from dumping subsidized agricultural products into Shire markets.
aftermath: The Shire's delegate gave the longest speech in founding-era Congress history at four hours and twelve minutes including a detailed account of every crop variety the Shire grows and why each one matters. Several delegates fell asleep. The resolution passed by a comfortable margin anyway because nobody wanted to be seen voting against hobbits and their vegetables.
waluigiComment: The Shire understands something most large nations do not: the moral weight of being obviously harmless is a political resource. Nobody wants to be the person who made the hobbits cry. Waluigi has studied this technique. Waluigi is not harmless enough to use it.

title: Data Merchants Information Sovereignty Act
description: Established that information about a nation's citizens, infrastructure, and governance collected within that nation's territory belongs to that nation regardless of who collected it. Targeted at Data Merchant and Internet Federation data collection practices.
aftermath: Failed by one vote after the Data Merchants lobbied heavily against their own proposed regulation, having initially proposed it as a negotiating position they expected to be amended. The amendment they wanted did not materialize. They voted against their own resolution. It failed. The data collection practices that motivated the resolution continue unchanged.
waluigiComment: The Data Merchants proposed a regulation they did not want passed, expecting negotiation, received no negotiation, and then voted against themselves. The result is that there are no rules. Waluigi is not sure whether to be impressed by the miscalculation or horrified by the outcome. Both, probably.

title: Dimensional Monitoring Defunding Act
description: Proposed immediate 60% reduction in funding for the Eyes of the Ring dimensional monitoring stations, citing high maintenance costs and lack of active threats.
aftermath: Passed by a razor-thin margin. Three months later the First Rift Leak occurred in the Subspace Sector. The Iron Pact utilized the resulting chaos to sell their own private security services to the nations whose monitoring they had just defunded.
waluigiComment: They did not defund it because it was expensive. They defunded it because the stations were pointed at Iron Pact shipyard projects. Efficiency. Crime pays better when nobody is looking.

title: Centennial Seat Freeze Resolution
proposedBy: Sovereignty Bloc joint proposal: Mushroom Kingdom, Gondor, Shake Kingdom, The Shire, Koopa Troop
description: Freeze current seat allocation for one hundred years until 1133 BF to prevent manipulation of population-tier seat counts through census disputes, territorial expansion, or demographic engineering.
aftermath: Motivated by three concurrent census disputes. The freeze solved the immediate crisis by making the crisis permanent. Nobody's seats can change which means nobody's seats are accurate which means everyone is equally unhappy. The sovereignty bloc supported it because it locked in their current advantage.
waluigiComment: The Centennial Freeze is the most Glazed Congress thing the Glazed Congress has ever done: solve a problem by agreeing to stop looking at the problem for a hundred years. Frozen seats mean frozen injustice. But unfrozen seats meant census manipulation. The Congress chose the known unfairness over the unknown unfairness. Waluigi disagrees. Waluigi understands.

title: Koopa Troop Conditional Full Membership
description: Application for full membership from the Koopa Troop, previously held in observer status pending observer. Conditional provisions required formal renunciation of castle-seizure practices and acknowledgment of Mushroom Kingdom territorial sovereignty.
aftermath: The Mushroom Kingdom's sponsorship was technically required under charter rules for nations with unresolved territorial disputes with existing members. The Mushroom Kingdom delegate looked physically pained during the entire proceeding. The Koopa Troop delegate appeared to find this entertaining. The conditions have been partially honored.
waluigiComment: Bowser attended in person for the vote. He is very large. The chamber seating had to be rearranged. He voted to admit himself which is not technically against the rules. He seemed pleased with himself. He is always pleased with himself. Waluigi has complicated feelings about Bowser. Mostly competitive ones.

title: Greenskin Territories Military Conduct Standards
description: Required the Greenskin Territories to adopt minimum standards for military conduct including prohibition on non-combatant targeting, restrictions on scorched-earth tactics, and mandatory reporting of cross-border military incursions.
aftermath: Failed to reach two-thirds threshold. The Greenskin Territories delegate's response speech was seven minutes long, contained no diplomatic language whatsoever, and was described by three separate attendees as the most honest thing ever said in the chamber. The standards were not adopted. The conduct has not changed.
waluigiComment: The Greenskin Territories Warchief said in seven minutes what most delegates spend seven hours obscuring: we have our way, you have yours, your rules are written to advantage you and disadvantage us, and we see what you are doing. He was right about all of it. The standards were also necessary. Both things were true simultaneously. The Congress could only process one.

title: Saddle Arabia Water Rights Compact
description: Framework for shared management of cross-border aquifers and river systems affecting multiple member territories in the central-southern Doughnut World. Included mandatory disclosure of water extraction rates, conservation targets, and arbitration for disputes.
aftermath: Saddle Arabia has been pushing water rights legislation since 1026 and finally achieved it through eight years of bilateral agreements that made the compact feel inevitable. The five no votes were from nations with upstream positions on shared waterways who stood to lose extraction flexibility. They have complied minimally.
waluigiComment: Eight years. Saddle Arabia came back every session with better data, more signatories to bilateral agreements, and more patience than any other delegation in this chamber. Waluigi has watched this process. Patience is a political strategy. It is a very slow one. It worked.

title: Rakasha Clans Mobile Census Methodology Amendment
description: Second attempt to reform census methodology for nomadic and semi-nomadic populations. Narrower scope than the 1027 attempt, specifically requesting that mobile populations be counted at primary seasonal settlement locations rather than excluded from counts entirely.
aftermath: Passed on the second attempt after eight years of steady lobbying. The methodology change did not affect seat allocation due to the Centennial Freeze but established better baseline data. The Rakasha Clans' population was found to be 34% higher than previous counts. This information is on record. It will matter in 1133 BF.
waluigiComment: The Rakasha Clans lost in 1027 and came back in 1035 with better arguments, a coalition partner, and a narrower ask. They won. The lesson: if you cannot win what you want, win what you can, record the result, and return. Waluigi has taken notes.

title: Internet Federation Holographic Presence Rules
description: Formal rules governing the Internet Federation's use of holographic delegates, remote voting systems, and digital presence protocols in Congress sessions. Several nations had raised objections to the Federation voting through systems they also managed.
aftermath: The Internet Federation proposed the rules themselves, which the Congress found suspicious. Examination revealed the proposed rules were actually quite fair and the Federation proposed them preemptively to prevent less favorable rules being imposed. This was clever. The Congress was grudgingly impressed.
waluigiComment: The Federation regulated themselves before anyone else could. This is the correct strategic move. Waluigi has recommended this approach to several nations with transparency problems. None of them have been clever enough to do it.

title: Peach Loyalist Observer Status Review
description: Review of whether the Peach Loyalists constituted a sufficiently distinct political entity from the Mushroom Kingdom to maintain separate observer status, following significant overlap in their diplomatic positions over ten years of sessions.
aftermath: Failed comprehensively. Most delegates saw no reason to reduce observer representation. Several noted privately that the Peach Loyalists had often taken positions the Mushroom Kingdom officially could not and that this functional independence had value. The Mushroom Kingdom withdrew the proposal without comment.
waluigiComment: The Mushroom Kingdom proposed stripping observer status from their own allies. This was either very stupid or very strategic depending on whether the Peach Loyalists were informed in advance. Based on the expression of the Peach Loyalist delegate during the vote, Waluigi has a theory about which one it was.

title: Iron Legion Full Membership Application
proposedBy: Iron Pact (joint: Regal Empire, Iron Hills faction delegates)
description: Application for the Iron Legion to transition from observer to full membership. Contested on grounds that the Iron Legion is a military organization not a nation-state and therefore cannot hold sovereign territory. Countered that the Iron Legion controls defined territorial installations across multiple regions.
aftermath: The most alarming vote since Mordor. The Iron Legion now has full voting rights despite being a military organization with no civilian population and no civilian governance. Their seats are exercised by military officers. The precedent this sets for future applications from armed non-state actors has not been formally discussed.
waluigiComment: The Congress admitted a military without a country. Read that again. A military. Without a country. With full voting rights. Waluigi was present. Waluigi objected. Waluigi's objection was noted in the minutes and nowhere else. The Iron Legion delegate shook Waluigi's hand afterward. It was not a comfortable handshake.

title: Beanbean Kingdom Trade Zone Expansion
description: Expansion of the Beanbean Kingdom's designated free-trade zone to include maritime routes through the northern Glaze Sea, with reduced tariff rates for participating nations and streamlined customs procedures.
aftermath: Near-unanimous. The Beanbean Kingdom remains the most broadly liked member nation in the Congress. They founded the Congress, they host the most sessions, they vote consistently with stated principles, and their coffee is excellent. The one no vote was from a nation whose merchant fleet competes with the Beanbean maritime routes and who has the dignity to be honest about it.
waluigiComment: Waluigi has never had a bad experience with a Beanbean Kingdom delegate. This is unusual. Waluigi is suspicious of it. But the policy is good and the coffee is excellent and Waluigi voted yes.

title: Fated Place Observer Status and Territorial Dispute Framework
description: Observer status for the Fated Place pending resolution of contested territorial claims. Established a framework for nations with unresolved territorial disputes to participate in Congress proceedings without those disputes being implicitly legitimized or delegitimized by their participation.
aftermath: Useful precedent. Three other nations with territorial disputes have since used the same framework to participate without resolving underlying claims. The disputes remain unresolved. The participation continues. This is probably better than the alternative.
waluigiComment: The Fated Place sent a delegate who said almost nothing for three sessions and then delivered a forty-minute legal argument that nobody could find a flaw in. Waluigi respects this approach. Preparation and patience. The Congress rewards both if you are willing to wait.

title: Cybernetic Collectives Enhanced Monitoring Provisions Challenge
description: Legal challenge to whether the enhanced monitoring provisions applied to Mordor under the Mordor Compromise could also be applied to the Cybernetic Collectives based on governance structure similarities. The Collectives argued the provisions were discriminatory against non-traditional governance forms.
aftermath: Failed. The Congress was not prepared to rule that Mordor-specific monitoring provisions were discriminatory because doing so would invalidate the Mordor Compromise entirely. The Cybernetic Collectives' legal argument was sound. The political consequences of agreeing with it were unacceptable. The Congress chose politics.
waluigiComment: The Collectives were right on the law. The Congress knew they were right on the law. The Congress voted no anyway. This is how institutions protect themselves from their own precedents. Waluigi has seen this before. Waluigi will see it again.

title: Gondor Succession Crisis Non-Interference Resolution
description: Following the contested transition from steward to king governance, Gondor requested a Congress resolution affirming non-interference in member nation internal succession processes and prohibiting other members from supporting rival claimants.
aftermath: Gondor got what they needed. The three no votes were from nations who had been quietly supporting the steward faction and did not want to commit to stopping. The non-interference provisions are now on the books. They have not been consistently followed but they exist as a reference point for future disputes.
waluigiComment: Gondor had a legitimate emergency and the Congress responded appropriately. Waluigi voted yes. This is what the Congress is supposed to do. Waluigi is noting this instance because these instances deserve noting as much as the failures do.

title: Team Rocket Full Membership Application
description: Third membership application from Team Rocket. First two failed on grounds of documented criminal operations within member territories. Third application submitted following claimed internal restructuring and submission of new territorial documentation for the Viridian City administrative zone.
aftermath: Failed by the largest margin of any membership vote. The Viridian City documentation was not accepted as evidence of sovereign territory. The Pokemon League's delegate submitted a forty-page objection. Three delegates who voted yes have not publicly explained why.
waluigiComment: Waluigi voted no. Waluigi will vote no on a fourth application if submitted. Waluigi has documentation. Waluigi does not keep documentation on most entities. The fact that Waluigi keeps documentation on Team Rocket should tell you something.

title: Sovereignty Exception for Pre-emptive Stabilization
description: Legal amendment allowing member nations to cross borders without formal declaration of war if imminent social collapse is detected in a neighbor. Designed to prevent another Blorbs outbreak.
aftermath: Passed under intense lobbying. Within a year this was used as the legal justification for the Stabilization of the East Glaze regions, effectively a quiet annexation by the Empire.
waluigiComment: It is a stabilization the same way a boot stabilizes an ant. They convinced the Progressive Bloc to vote for it by calling it a humanitarian intervention. Everyone is so easily fooled by a good font.

title: Iron Hills Independent Arbitration Tribunal
description: Establishment of an independent arbitration tribunal for commercial disputes between member nations, with binding authority over signatories who agreed to its jurisdiction. Separate from the Congress's existing dispute resolution framework.
aftermath: The Iron Hills have been building parallel institutional infrastructure for years. This tribunal now handles more commercial disputes than the official Congress mechanism and is generally considered more efficient. Some members find the Iron Hills' institutional empire-building concerning. Most members just use the tribunal because it works.
waluigiComment: The Iron Hills are doing quietly what the Regal Empire does loudly. Building systems that make others dependent on you is a form of power that does not require armies. Waluigi respects it more than the army approach. Waluigi is still watching it carefully.

title: Greenskin Territories Medical Access Emergency Resolution
description: Emergency resolution allowing Blorbs medical teams to operate in Greenskin Territory border regions following outbreak reports, despite the Greenskin Territories not having signed the 1027 Blorbs Response Framework.
aftermath: Unanimous effective vote. The Greenskin Territories did not vote against despite not having signed the framework. They allowed access. The outbreak was contained. The Greenskin Territories have not since signed the framework. They have not since refused access during an emergency. This is a practical arrangement that works for unclear reasons.
waluigiComment: The Greenskin Warchief allowed the medical teams in and told nobody he had done so. He did not want it recorded that he cooperated with a Congress framework. He cooperated with the Congress framework. The people are alive. The record is ambiguous. Waluigi finds this quietly moving.

title: Warioland Mining Operations Environmental Standards
description: Required Warioland mining operations near DK Crew island territories to comply with minimum environmental standards following documented damage to shared coral reef ecosystems.
aftermath: Passed. Wario's delegate delivered a seventeen-minute speech about the economic importance of his mining operations. The coral reef data was projected behind him the entire time. The visual contrast was noted. Warioland has nominally complied. The compliance inspections have found mixed results.
waluigiComment: Donkey Kong sat in the front row for the entire session with his arms crossed. He did not speak once. He did not need to. Waluigi considers this excellent tactical restraint. The coral reefs are still damaged. The standards are on the books. Progress is slow and incomplete. This describes most things.

title: Raventree Fracture Emergency Response Authorization
proposedBy: Mages Guild (observer advisory) / multiple member sponsors
description: Emergency authorization for cross-border response to the Raventree Fracture dimensional event. Included temporary suspension of standard border protocols, authorization for Mages Guild personnel to operate across all member territories, and emergency funding reallocation.
aftermath: Unanimous effective vote achieved faster than any previous emergency resolution. Unfortunately unanimity and speed cannot substitute for the fourteen years of dimensional monitoring baseline data the Congress chose to defund in 1031 BF. Response teams are working blind. The emergency authorization is the right response to a crisis that did not have to be this bad.
waluigiComment: They agreed unanimously when it was too late. They disagreed when it mattered. Waluigi is sitting in the chamber watching them congratulate themselves on rapid emergency response to an emergency that their own vote in 1031 BF made catastrophically worse. Waluigi is not going to say I told you so. Waluigi is going to sit here and not say it very loudly.

title: Regal Empire Iron Mandate Observer Investigation
proposedBy: Beanbean Kingdom / Gondor / Shake Kingdom / Pokemon League / Yoshi's Island / Iron Hills / Saddle Arabia (joint)
description: Authorization of an independent observer investigation into the Regal Empire's Iron Mandate legislation and its compatibility with the Species Recognition Compact, specifically regarding supernatural persecution provisions.
aftermath: An investigation, not a condemnation. Seven nations who would vote yes on an investigation voted no on the earlier condemnation draft. This is the compromise: look at the problem officially without committing to doing anything about what you find. The investigation team has been named. The Regal Empire has not blocked them. Yet.
waluigiComment: An investigation is not a condemnation. It is a promise to maybe consider a condemnation at a future date after reviewing findings that everyone already knows. Waluigi voted yes because an investigation is better than nothing. Waluigi will not pretend an investigation is the same as accountability.

title: Emergency Taxation of Neutral Trade Routes
description: Levying a 15% toll on all non-aligned merchant vessels passing through the Great Glaze Bridge to fund Congress security forces.
aftermath: Caused a massive trade strike. Smaller nations and the Non-Aligned bloc are currently suing the Congress in its own court, which is conveniently funded by the same tax.
waluigiComment: Finally the Congress is becoming a real government: they have learned how to take money from people who do not have a seat at the table. Waluigi is almost proud.

title: Iron Mandate Condemnation Resolution
description: Challenge to the Regal Empire's Iron Mandate legislation granting Iron Legion emergency powers, argued to violate Species Recognition Compact through supernatural persecution provisions.
aftermath: Challenge is valid. Congress has the votes to pass. Iron Pact has made clear condemnation would be treated as hostile action against a founding member. Smaller nations calculating whether economic dependence on Regal Empire trade makes voting a risk they can afford. Vote date not yet scheduled.
waluigiComment: The Congress has the votes. The Congress does not have the courage. These are different things. Waluigi has watched this pattern before. The votes exist. The will does not. By the time the will arrives the damage is done.
